name: Slack Huddles
description: Slack Huddles provides live audio and video conversations inside Slack channels and direct messages, with screen sharing, notes, reactions, and optional transcripts or AI notes where plans and policies permit.
agentUseSummary: Slack Huddles cannot be connected directly to Relay agents because Slack publishes no Huddles method family, Huddles-specific OAuth scope, remote MCP service, or supported contract to start, join, inspect, transcribe, or administer native Huddles.

blocked.label: Connect Slack Huddles
blocked.description: Slack does not publish an application authorization contract for operating or reading native Huddles.

blocked.label: Start, join, or control Huddles
blocked.description: Slack publishes no supported method to start, join, end, invite to, record, or otherwise control a native Huddle.

blocked.label: Read Huddle content
blocked.description: Relay does not discover or download native Huddle audio, video, screen shares, transcripts, summaries, canvases, or participant activity through adjacent file and conversation APIs.

blocked.label: Automate the Slack client
blocked.description: Relay Console cannot reuse a user's Slack session, invoke private client endpoints, drive Huddle UI, or capture media traffic.

blocked.label: Substitute adjacent Slack APIs
blocked.description: The third-party Calls API, generic user huddle-status event, conversation fields, file fields, and Enterprise audit events are not a native Huddles product API and cannot be presented as one.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Slack Huddles actions can be enabled until Slack publishes a supported distributable Huddles API or remote MCP service.

runtimeSupport.description: No documented public Slack Huddles API or remote MCP service is available to mount as OpenClaw tools.
No documented public Slack Huddles API or remote MCP service is available to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Slack exposes native Huddles through its clients. The official developer method and scope catalogs publish no Huddles family or Huddles-specific authorization, and adjacent status, conversation, file, audit-log, and third-party Calls interfaces do not provide a supported native Huddles integration contract.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request a Slack token or signing secret for native Huddles and do not show Connect. Reconsider only if Slack publishes an officially supported native Huddles API or remote MCP service for third-party applications.

evidence.supports: Slack documents native Huddles as a user-facing live audio and video feature operated from Slack conversations.
Slack's official Web API method catalog includes Calls, canvases, conversations, files, Lists, and other families but no native Huddles method family.
Slack's official scope catalog publishes no Huddles-specific bot, user, configuration, or app-level scope.
Slack explicitly documents the Calls API as a way for third-party call apps to register their own calls in Slack, not an API for native Slack Huddles.
Slack's huddle-status event is a generic user-change payload requiring users:read; it exposes a user's status change rather than a native Huddle resource or control surface.
Enterprise audit logs enumerate Huddle lifecycle actions for governance records but do not provide a native Huddles operational or content API.
